newsitem.title: CANADA: Westcoast losing Canada firm service shippers.
newsitem.headline: Westcoast losing Canada firm service shippers.

text.p: Westcoast Energy Inc, the main mover of natural gas in British Columbia, said on Friday that several of its shippers chose not to renew portions of their firm transport contracts starting on November 1, 1997.
Westcoast said the affected gas transport volumes ammounted to 470 million cubic feet per day, including 166 MMCFD on the southern portion of its B.C. pipeline system.
The affected volumes represent 12 percent of current contracted capacity.
"Having received these notices, we will now talk to new customers to place capacity on our mainline over the next year," Westcoast pipeline division president Al Edgeworth said in a statement.
"We also believe that some producers may move from firm to interruptible service to give them more flexibility in the current low gas price environment."
Edgeworth said also that the company was pursuing discussions with its shippers with the aim of restructuring the regulatory basis of Westcoast's pipeline and field services businesses.
He said Westcoast would like to put in place an incentive-based regulatory scheme "which would offer more innovative solutions to individual customers."

Several other Canadian pipeline companies, including TransCanada PipeLines Ltd, IPL Energy Inc and NOVA Corp are in various stages of instituting incentive ratemaking programs. -- Reuters Calgary Bureau 403 531-1624
